 Serie A Preview: Parma vs Roma – Team News, Lineups & Prediction 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Stadio Ennio Tardini sets the stage for a ‘David vs Goliath’ Serie A clash between Parma and Roma. Although the two sides find themselves on opposite sides of the table, the stakes could hardly be any higher for either team. 
 Parma sacked underperforming manager Carlos Cuesta just after the previous international break, but new boss Alberto Gilardino has struggled to drag the Crusaders out of trouble in the infancy of his tenure. The 44-year-old has lost four of his first six league games in charge of the club (W1, D1).
 OneFootball Videos
 As a result, the Crusaders sit just a point clear of 18th-placed Monza. Gilardino has yet to address Parma’s significant scoring problems, as they head into proceedings as one of just two Serie A sides yet to hit double digits this season (9). In stark contrast, Roma are the only team to smash a 30-goal milestone after 11 games (31).
 Gian Piero Gasperini’s men thrashed Sassuolo 3-0 on the stroke of November’s international break, extending their unbeaten league run to 18 matches. That’s just one shy of the club’s best-ever streak in Serie A, which means this could potentially be a landmark occasion for Roma, who trail early pacesetters Lazio by only two points ahead of Saturday’s kickoff.
 Match Preview
 Parma 
 An early red card led to Parma’s 2-1 home defeat to Bologna last time out, deepening the Crusaders’ crisis at the Tardini. Gilardino’s charges have picked up just a single win from their last seven home outings (D2, L4), failing to find the net four times in that sequence. On that basis, an unlikely win against Roma looks even more far-fetched.
 Speaking of which, Parma bring an ominous four-game losing run against the Giallorossi into this encounter. They’ve also lost six of their last eight home meetings with Roma (W2), including a dramatic 3-2 loss in the corresponding fixture in 2025/26, further highlighting the magnitude of the task awaiting them on Saturday.
 In search of good omens, Parma avoided relegation last season despite having just 13 points after 11 matches, just as they do now. Interestingly, the hosts will be desperate for history to repeat itself, having claimed one of their only 11 league victories last season on Matchday 12.
 Roma 
 November’s international break came at an inopportune moment for Roma. Gasperini’s men were on a three-game winning league run before the pause halted their momentum, but they’ll be confident of continuing in the same vein at the Tardini. Adding to this sentiment, they remain one of just three Serie A teams yet to lose on the road this term (W3, D2).
 All that has made Roma fans dream of the first Scudetto since the beginning of the 21st century. However, Gasperini must find a way to tighten up his side’s defense if he is to beat Inter and Lazio to the punch. Indeed, the Giallorossi have conceded at least two goals in each of their last three away games in all competitions (W1, D1, L1), canceling out their well-documented scoring prowess.
 On the bright side, the visitors have been quick out of the blocks this season. Roma have led at half-time in a joint-league-high seven matches (HT: D3, L1). Taking another early lead would probably bolster their chances of claiming three points here, although it’s worth noting that they’ve conceded precisely two goals on three of their last four Serie A visits to the Tardini.
 Team News
 Parma could be missing several first-team stars for this showdown. In addition to suspended defender Abdoulaye Ndiaye and injured striker David Romero, Gilardino may also be without injury-prone midfielder Adrian Bernabe and experienced center-back Diego Carlos.
 As for Roma, only former captain Lorenzo Pellegrini won’t be at Gasperini’s disposal. Paulo Dybala and Mile Svilar both resumed full training during the international break, with the latter expected to immediately reclaim his place between the sticks. Meanwhile, Matias Soule and Rodrigo Mora are likely to start in attack behind free-firing Donyell Malen.
 Parma vs Roma Potential Starting Lineups
 Parma (3-5-2): Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Drobnic; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Lontani, Toure.
 Roma (3-4-2-1): Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Soule, Mora; Malen.
 Parma vs Roma Prediction
 There’s no doubt that a point here would be huge for Parma. However, it’s hard to imagine the misfiring hosts matching Roma’s high intensity and unparalleled scoring potential. As such, we expect the visitors to pick up where they left off before the break.
